questions.question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

I suggested her two ________ dates, both in the coming month and just a few days ________ from each other to start her singing practice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is-'alternative, apart'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's check each option:
 
 
• Option 1:

 
 
• alarming: that makes you frightened or worried
 
• near: not far away in time or distance; close
 
 
 
• Option 2:
 
 
• adverse: making something difficult for somebody
 
• different: not the same
 
 
 
• Option 3:
 
 
• **alternative**: that you can use do, etc., instead of something else
 
• **apart**: away from somebody/something or each other; not together
 
 
 
• Option 4:
 
 
• alternating: to cause two types of events or things to happen or regularly follow one after the other
 
• closely: without a big difference between two people, groups, or things
 
 
 
 Hence, the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks is 'alternative, apart'.
 
• Thus, *option 3 *is the correct answer.

 

The correct sentence is:* **I suggested her two **alternative** dates, both in the coming month and just a few days **apart**__ from each other, to start her singing practice.*

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. People can get in touch with the larger global community by communicating and sharing their views via social media.

B. Furthermore, this provides a suitable platform to express their views, conduct business with online transaction, or find new people or jobs.

C. Smartphones have become a very important form of communication these days.

D. It is impossible for a rational person to deny the advantages of smartphones as they are devices suitable for a wide variety of tasks.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "CDAB"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The jumbled sentences can be solved by what exactly the topic is and where it leads to.
 
• Rearrange the sentences in a sequence as per the events that happened.

• There are four jumbled arrangements in the options given.
 
• Find which Option comes first and mark the answer according to that.
 
• Options 3 and 4 don't synchronize but for Options 1 and 2, we can focus as it starts with the Smartphone the root of the topic.
 
• Option 2 has a systematic arrangement of the sentence like the Smartphone as a communication device, the advantages, a suitable platform to explore new feeds and finally the worldwide impact of social media.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Children like to play games all the time.

options.text: Children like being played to games all the time.
Games liked playing with children all the time.
Games are liked to be played by children all the time.
Children are being played games all the time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Games are liked to be played by children all the time**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **active form** of a sentence is changed to its **passive form** by **interchanging the object and subject**. 
 
• In the sentence "**Children like to play games all the time**", "**all the time**" is the **adjunct** which does **not undergo any changes**. 
 
• In "Children like to play games", "**Children**" is the **subject**, "**like**" is the **verb** and "**to play games**" is the **object**. 
 
• The **passive **of it will be "**Games are liked to be played by children**".
 
• If the **adjunct **is also added, the complete sentence is "**Games are liked to be played by the children all the time**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **sentence** can be divided into **Subject, Verb and Object**.

 
 
• **Example:** *Adam eats chocolates*.
 
 
 
• The **subject** is usually the **noun**. It denotes the **actor** of the action. Here,"**Adam**" is the subject.
 
• The **verb** is also referred to as the **Predicate**. It denotes **action**. In the given sentence, "**eats**" is the verb.
 
• **Object** denotes the **sufferer** of the action. Here, "**chocolates**" is the object.

questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

One must care __as for family members__ as possible.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**as much for family members**". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**As for family members**" means caring for the family member **without any emotion**. 
 
• **"Much"**, being a **determiner** means to a **great extent**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Rita likes this dress very **much**.* 
 
 
 
• "**As much for family members**" means **caring** for the family members to a **great extent**. 
 
• It adds more **meaning** and **depth** to the sentence.
 
• Therefore, the appropriate option is "as much for family members". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Determiners** are used in **referring and quantifying.**
 
• **Referring** means it points to the **referent** of the noun and **Quantifying** means it denotes the **quantity**.
 
• **Determiners** can basically be divided into **articles, demonstrative and personal**. 
 
• **Articles** - a, an, the.
 
 
• **Example:** *I had **an** awful day. *
 
 
 
• **Demonstrative** - this, that, these, those.
 
 
• **Example:** *He wants **this** book.*
 
 
 
• **Personal** - my, his, their.
 
 
• **Example:** *Both **my** children are playing. *
